name: Hearthroot
summary: The hub town of the Ylden: a stone town carved into the Tree's roots, warm with lamplight and starving. No leaves have fallen for nine years, so its leaf-mould fields are dead and the Fountain of Hearthroot has stood dry. Each spring the hero restores fills the fountain by a third, and the town comes back to life around it.
look: Grey, rough-cut stone bricks with a pale flagstone lip, laced with dark root fibres and creeping ivy where the Tree grows through the masonry. The town sits inside a vast root cavern whose air is a warm, dark plum-brown. Far back, a skyline of stone houses steps along a ridge: gables, hipped roofs, lean-tos, narrow towers and the odd battlement, each house lit on its west face and dark on its east, chimneys on some, small amber windows glowing. Nearer, great roots arch overhead with lanterns hanging from them, each in a faint ring of light. From the stone ceiling hang chains, red swallowtail banners with gold emblems, iron lamps and plank platforms slung on chains. Pale volumetric shafts of light slant down through the dark, and warm dust motes drift in them. Wall sconces throw soft pools of amber onto the stone. Shops are small root-wrapped huts and timber stalls: a smithy with a glowing forge, a dyer under hanging bolts of coloured cloth, a grocer under a striped awning, a map-maker with a brass telescope. A dark fringe of fence posts and rafter ends frames the bottom and top of the frame.

name: Heartwood
summary: Tunnels through the living wood under Hearthroot, lit by glowing fungus and running with amber sap. Rot Dwarves, Amberlee miners the stillglass held and let go, walk its halls, and the grub Gnarlmaw gnaws the taproot dry. It is damp, dim and alive, with the hollow town of Amberlee in its middle.
look: The walls are red-brown living wood with long vertical strands of grain, its top edges capped with a sculpted fringe of dark moss and grass, and its undersides trailing orange rootlets and clumps of moss. The tunnels open into tall hollows whose far wall is a braid of great wood fibres, some hanging from the roof, some rising from the floor, each leaning its own way, sunk in a deep green-teal gloom. Nearer, hanging roots and rooted columns carry glowing fungus caps at their tips. Faint cyan spores float everywhere, a few larger and haloed. On the floor grow clusters of glowing cyan mushrooms, small orange toadstools and tufts of fern; amber shelf fungus glows on the walls. Pools of golden sap lie in the floor and slow the feet, and at Amber Falls a sheet of sap pours from a split in the heartwood. Mossy green timber trestles and plank platforms hung on ropes cross the open air. Pale green light shafts fall from above. A dark fringe of fern and root silhouettes sits along the bottom of the frame.

name: Hollin Tower
summary: The Hollin dwarves' mining tower, bolted into the trunk of the Ylden, and their city Kettleforge inside it. Its gears, winches and ore roads have stood still since the dwarves went quiet, and the Iron Dwarves still guard the works on their king's last order. A long vertical climb of iron, stone and cold forges.
look: Cut stone plates a tile wide in cool blue-violet grey, some pitted, framed by riveted iron girders. The halls are tall and dark. Far back, the tower's shafts stand in three storeys, each on a gallery floor with a lit lip and a railing, and great gears turn slowly in the dark between them, with sparks and lamp glints. Nearer, lattice trusses hang from the roof to their own depths, each ending in a pulley block and hook, and bolted posts rise from the floor to carry beams on knee braces. Chains hang everywhere. Small hanging lamps and wall lamps burn lamp orange, each throwing a soft pool on the stone, and pale light shafts slant through the dust. Rust streaks the iron. Platforms are iron-framed trestles with grey ash planks, and plank ledges hang on chains. The Smelter's great crucible pours a white-hot stream into a glowing trough; the Gear Pit's rusted gears with brass hubs stand in its back wall. A dark fringe of rubble and crag silhouettes runs along the bottom.

name: The Haar
summary: A marsh on the Tree's lower limbs, drowned in a grey-green fog that is the Haar Wyrm's steam cooled over the water. Rotting boardwalks run between lamp-lit pockets, and the lamp town of Lampwick and the stilt town of Polesend keep their lights burning for the miners who came back as Drowned Dwarves. Fog limits what you can see; lanterns part it.
look: Everything sinks into a thick grey-green fog. The footing is old, bone-pale umber limb wood with a cool moss and grass fringe, and boardwalks of grey reed planks on posts. The fog hides most of the room, and every light clears a wavering, uneven pocket around it: lamp posts with a lantern on an iron arm, lanterns hung on cords, a shrine, a hag's green wisp. Far back, the drowned limbs of the Tree reach across a green murk, paler the lower they sit, with will-o'-lanterns glimmering far off. Nearer, bare crooked limbs reach in from the sides, hung with long ragged moss beards that drip. Bands of fog drift slowly across the scene in layers. Black water lies in the low places, with iron spikes under it. Boardwalk houses have reed-grey plank walls, damp dark frames and warm yellow windows. Lantern yellow is the only warm colour. A dark fringe of reeds and mud mounds sits along the bottom of the frame.

name: High Boughs
summary: The sunlit canopy of the Ylden, above the fog: boughs as wide as roads, leaves taller than houses, and wind. The elves of Sylvarre live where the boughs meet, many of them glad of the endless summer. Wind currents carry you across open sky, and ripe seed-pods throw you high.

Behind, the air is a pale green-blue haze: far boughs with leaves bunched along them, a ridge of pointed fir-like crowns fading into valley mist, and flat-bottomed clouds lit on top. Nearer, great boughs cross in from the sides hung with enormous pointed leaves with pale midribs. Vines with leaf clumps hang from the bark ceiling. Bands of wind show as a faint wash of sky with gusts racing downwind and torn leaves tumbling in them. Ripe seed-pods sit on the ground like plump pale-gold ribbed gourds held by green sepals. Planks of reddish wood hang on ropes and stand on built trestles. Thorny brambles hold red-tipped thorn bulbs. Soft sun shafts fall through, and the colours are leaf green, sky blue and cloud white. A dark fringe of fern and leaf silhouettes runs along the bottom.

name: Storm Spires
summary: Above the leaves the Ylden's crown breaks into islands of stone adrift in a violet storm, where the elves built lightning shrines and a great bridge before the storm came. Carillon, the bell town, stands on the last great island, warm and rain-soaked, its bells ringing only when the wind remembers. Past it the Spires climb by dead copper conduits to the Roost, where Skyrend nests on the Sky Spring. The mood is wind, rain and old elven grandeur gone to ruin.
look: The play plane is pale grey-lavender ashlar shrine stone, laid in courses with gold inlay and capped with a ragged lip of storm-wet green grass: causeways, broken pillars, shrine floors and floating spans of masonry, each span hanging a jagged cone of violet-magenta rock with roots trailing from it. The sky is a dark storm ramp from deep blue-violet down to a bruised wine, with heavy mauve cloud banks. Far back, a ruined elven city stands on a terraced hill: needle spires under cones, notched crowns, towers sheared off at a slant, broad keeps, some joined by pointed-arch bridges, a few slit windows lit ember orange. Nearer, sky islands drift: rounded bellies of chunky lit stone under grass lips, some carrying a ruined tower with one warm window. Dim threads of violet lightning flicker in the far layer; only lightning on the play plane is bright. Wind-slanted rain falls in two depths, splashes in small crowns on open tops and leaves a broken pale sheen on wet stone, while ground under an overhang stays dry. Elven lamps hang from the ceilings in warm pools of light, and storm crystals bristle on the cliffs. The foreground fringe is a low, dark broken fence of timber stubs and a sagging rail. The whole frame carries a warm hearth haze and grade.

name: Vorrhallow
summary: The drowned capital of the Hollin dwarves, held still in the moment of its flooding while magenta stillglass forces through its masonry. Colonnades, a market, kennels and a throne hall stand in still teal water, with a tide line on every stone at the height of a dwarf's beard. It is the quietest, saddest place in the Tree: a dirge, falling drops and the hum of crystal. Once Thane Vorrund weeps, the Drowned Market wakes as the last town before the Evercrown.
look: Squat, heavy dwarf masonry in a cool grey-lavender, laid in large courses on a footing with a string course, every block marked by a teal tide line where the flood stood and capped with teal waterweed. Clusters of magenta stillglass break out of joints and pillar faces: prism shards broad at the root with a lit facet and a shaded one, a crust of wine-dark glass over their roots, and lit seams of glass running back into the stone. Vaults spring from pillars with wide capitals; some have fallen in and lie as heaps in the water. Behind the play plane a sunken great hall recedes into a drowned-blue haze: colossal pillars and round arches, crystal clusters glowing on the far walls, and a dark ridge of great crystal masses rising from below. Still, shallow teal water lies across the hall floors, mirroring pillars, foes and the hero upside down, with spiked pits under it. Falls of time-locked water pour in sheets. Light comes in faint shafts from above, from the glass's own magenta glow pooling on the stone, and from the cyan rune of a shrine. Crystal dust hangs in the air and drops fall from crystal stalactites. The foreground fringe is a low row of dark crystal shards.

name: Sunken Spring
summary: An optional zone under Vorrhallow and the first source of every spring in the Tree: a drowned cistern, the dwarves' old aqueduct and the deep pool where the Drowned Warden keeps the Source. Most of it is swum. It is cold, deep and hushed, lit by the spring's own pale light rising through the water.
look: Warm umber travertine ashlar, laid by dwarf masons in courses of broken bond, each block lit on its top and left edge, with chipped corners, clumps of moss in the bed joints and blue-green mineral drips hanging from the joints. Vaults spring low from hanging piers broken off unevenly at the foot; snapped arch tops stand as stepped wedges at the waterline over pier stumps on the bed. Most of each room is deep water: a teal that darkens in steps toward an abyss blue-black, with an ordered dither in its depth, wavering caustic light just under the surface, a mirrored band of the room above it, and drowned stone that dims and wavers below the line. Specks of light and bubbles rise through it. Behind, a flooded cavern of stepped rimstone pools under slanting shafts of light recedes into a pale slate haze, with a row of aqueduct arches on piers and weed swaying up from the bottom. In the aqueduct a broken channel pours a fall of threaded water from the vault, breaking into a boil of white water, spray, foam lace and climbing mist. Domes of trapped air hold dry stone shelves. The foreground fringe is a low dark row of reeds.

name: The Evercrown
summary: The inside of the Everbloom at the Tree's crown, and the last climb: warm living stillglass that breathes. Corrupted foes from every zone guard its shelves, pockets of wrong gravity lift you up its shafts, and the Proving Scar asks for every ability before the throne, the veins and the heart. It feels alien and bodily, a heartbeat under everything and cyan light in black-violet flesh.
look: The play plane is a mass of rounded cells of black-violet scar tissue, laid like cobbles of flesh, seamed with wine-dark sinew and cooler blue seams, each cell rimmed with cyan light from a small glowing pore. Ledges are grown shelves: a lit top band over rounded lobes, a fleshy root hanging under each with a bead of cyan sap, slung on strands of sinew. Behind, a ribbed far wall of dark wine flesh recedes into a deep wine haze, with great crystal masses rising from below and long magenta stillglass tendrils hanging and curling down, each tipped with a cyan bulb. Columns of wrong gravity rise as violet light with cyan motes drifting upward through them. In the Veins a braided stalk climbs the back of the shaft, carrying beads of light up channels to a crystal eye-flower at the vault. Polyps, wall eyes and short crystal floor stubs crowd the edges, and cyan spore motes float everywhere. Red appears only on what hurts: fire seals of tall licking flame, thorn bulbs and a foe's tell. Deep solid mass sinks to near-black, crossed by faint zigzag crystal veins. The foreground fringe is a low row of dark crystal shards.

name: Inner Rings
summary: An abstract trial space off the map, inside the Tree's oldest growth rings, reached through a Ringreader's menu. Six timed courses of pure platforming over spikes, each ending at a bronze bell; a hazard costs time, never health. It is pale, quiet and nearly monochrome, a place outside the world's weather.
look: Pale grey masonry with a faint lavender cast and no moss or warmth: clean ashlar ledges and slim pillars standing over beds of steel floor spikes with a double rim. Behind the play plane is a dark slate void with nothing alive in it: great faint broken rings drawn as dotted arcs, pale stone slabs hanging motionless at different depths, a jagged ridge of broken grey stone low in the distance, and soft slanting shafts of pale light. Pale flecks drift in the air and ride the wind currents in place of leaves. Chains hang from the ceiling and a few sconces glow on the walls. Thorn bulbs grow from dark brambles in the gaps. In the Ring of Stillness, curtains and falls of teal time-locked water pour down out of the void. The bell at each course's end hangs in a stone frame with a slow warm glow, the only warm light in the space. Deep solid mass falls off into near-black with faint level bedding seams. The foreground fringe is a low row of dark rock rubble. The whole frame carries a bare grey-stone haze and grade.
